summary: Backend-only testing of 2-layer badge system (TRUST + COMMERCIAL) and /api/stats/claims-monthly. New test file /app/backend/tests/test_badge_system.py with 17 cases — ALL PASS. Regression: iteration_9 V2-seed+geocode suite re-run, 17/17 still PASS. Verified end-to-end: (a) /api/search/smart?q=urologie returns `badges` (trust+commercial) and `is_sponsored` on every result; (b) uro-ci-001 carries trust=verified/emerald/level=3 AND commercial=premium/purple AND is_sponsored=true; (c) /api/providers/{id}/master returns same badges + is_sponsored; (d) /api/providers/search?q=urologie includes badges on every result; (e) /api/stats/claims-monthly is public (no auth), returns {month yyyy-mm, claims_this_month>=0, verified_total>=0, providers_total>0}; (f) badges are idempotent across repeated calls; (g) ranking sanity: verified+premium (uro-ci-001) is well-ranked (top half) but does NOT dominate — top-3 is not 100% sponsored; (h) unit tests on compute_badges confirm expired tier_until falls back to free, missing master_profile.commercial does NOT throw 500, verified flag overrides claim_status=pending, trust_score_bonus capped at 18.
action_items: None required — every spec item in the review request passes.
Optional: surface a `badges_legend` GET endpoint so the frontend can display the legend without duplicating the label/color map (currently hardcoded in services/badge.py only).
Optional: add a structured 'sponsored' disclaimer field (e.g. badges.disclaimer_text) so the UI can show a translatable 'Cette fiche est sponsorisée' line without inferring it from is_sponsored.
critical_code_review_comments: services/badge.py is clean (160 lines), well-documented, has a single source of truth for labels/colors and the +18 ranking bonus cap is explicit and defensible. _commercial_tier() correctly auto-expires past tier_until via fromisoformat with 'Z'→'+00:00' fix.

server.py L1591 uses `-trust_score_bonus(p)` as a ranking delta (negative because lower _rank() score = better) — verified by ranking sanity test: uro-ci-001 (verified+premium, +18 bonus) sits in top half but does NOT force #1, so proximity/triage_priority remain dominant. This matches the product transparency principle stated in the review brief.

compute_badges() is fully defensive: missing master_profile, missing commercial, malformed tier_until, unknown tier strings — all return safe defaults (trust=seeded, commercial=None). Confirmed by 7 unit tests including retrocompat case.

/api/stats/claims-monthly correctly uses ISO string for $gte on `created_at`. Note: this assumes claims.created_at is stored as ISO string (string comparison works only because ISO-8601 is lexicographically ordered). If a future writer ever stores a BSON Date instead, the comparison will silently return 0. Consider documenting this convention or coercing to a single type at write-time.
/api/providers/{id}/master correctly returns `is_sponsored: bool(badges.get('commercial'))` — matches is_sponsored definition in inject_badges() so list and detail endpoints stay consistent.

server.py is now 4299 lines (+50 since iteration_9). Modularization still recommended — /api/stats/* would be a natural fit for a routers/stats.py module alongside the suggested routers/admin_seed.py.

Two `from datetime import ...` imports inside functions (badge.py L86 indirectly via fromisoformat, server.py L4213). Move to module-level imports to avoid micro-cost per request — purely cosmetic, no functional impact.
